🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P1]** Return `PROVIDER_NOT_READY` while assignments for a changed context are pending, and add a test that pins the withholding. With an enabled mode, `resolve` evaluates against `requestedEvaluationContext`. Assignments fetched for a previous context are not used, so each flag returns the default until the new assignments arrive. That also applies to subjects without `dd_experimentation_opt_out_at`, and that is the intended behaviour. The error code in that state is `INVALID_CONTEXT`, from `selectPrecomputedFlagsConfiguration` (`precomputed-evaluation.ts:90-97`). Android and iOS return `PROVIDER_NOT_READY` for the same state. A malformed timestamp also returns `INVALID_CONTEXT`, so the code alone does not tell a customer which case occurred. No test pins the withholding for a subject without the attribute.
Evidence — what each SDK returns while subject B is pending Subject A is installed, then the context changes to subject B. Neither has the attribute. B's fetch is pending. | SDK | enabled mode | disabled mode | | --- | --- | --- | | JS (this PR) | default, `INVALID_CONTEXT` | A's value | | Android | default, `PROVIDER_NOT_READY` | A's value | | iOS | default, `providerNotReady` | A's value | `packages/browser/test/openfeature/experimentation-opt-out.spec.ts:355` asserts `INVALID_CONTEXT` for a pending opted-out subject. A mutant that serves the installed assignments to a subject without the attribute passed all 514 browser tests.
Suggested fix — remap only a well-formed context's INVALID_CONTEXT The core returns `INVALID_CONTEXT` for a context mismatch, a missing acknowledgement, or a malformed timestamp. The remap covers the first two only. `PARSE_ERROR` and `PROVIDER_NOT_READY` from the core pass through unchanged. The disabled path becomes identical to `main`. The remap stays until assignments for the requested context are installed, including after a failed refresh, as on Android and iOS. ```diff diff --git a/packages/browser/src/openfeature/provider.ts b/packages/browser/src/openfeature/provider.ts index 8d11292..1556a8f 100644 --- a/packages/browser/src/openfeature/provider.ts +++ b/packages/browser/src/openfeature/provider.ts @@ -16,7 +16,7 @@ import type { ProviderMetadata, ResolutionDetails, } from '@openfeature/web-sdk' -import { InvalidContextError, ProviderEvents, ProviderStatus } from '@openfeature/web-sdk' +import { ErrorCode, InvalidContextError, ProviderEvents, ProviderStatus } from '@openfeature/web-sdk' import { hasIndexedDB } from '../cache/helpers' import { IndexedDBFlagsCache } from '../cache/indexeddb-flags-cache' import { @@ -301,21 +301,41 @@ export class DatadogProvider extends DatadogProviderBase { _context: EvaluationContext, _logger: Logger ): ResolutionDetails> { - const context = - this.experimentationOptOutMode !== ExperimentationOptOutMode.Disabled - ? { + ...result, + errorCode: ErrorCode.PROVIDER_NOT_READY, + errorMessage: 'Assignments for the current evaluation context are not available', + } + : result, this.telemetryPolicy, - this.experimentationOptOutMode !== ExperimentationOptOutMode.Disabled ? Docs — README text for the same behaviour Suggested addition under "Experimentation opt-out" in `packages/browser/README.md`: ```markdown With either enabled mode, the provider does not use assignments fetched for a different context, for any subject, including subjects without `dd_experimentation_opt_out_at`. During a context change, flags return the application default with `PROVIDER_NOT_READY` until assignments for the new context arrive, unless a configuration without a context (for example an `initialFlagsConfiguration`) applies to the subject. A malformed timestamp returns `INVALID_CONTEXT` instead. With `Disabled`, the previous assignments remain available during the change. ```
Verification — what I ran - Browser 516/516 in the batch with the other suggestions from this review, including the three new or changed tests. - With the remap disabled, 3 tests fail: the new withholding test and both rows of `uses the requested subject while pending`. - My first version of this fix tested for a context mismatch instead. It replaced `PARSE_ERROR` with `PROVIDER_NOT_READY` for an unreadable `initialFlagsConfiguration`. The first new test guards that case.

🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P1]** Validate activation timestamps only for an opted-out subject in `FutureExperimentsOnly` mode. This check runs on every rules evaluation that reaches allocation selection, in every mode. It parses each `randomizationActivatedAt` that is present until one fails. The Node server SDK uses this evaluator and passes no mode (`packages/node-server/src/provider.ts:147`), so server customers pay this cost with opt-out off once the backend sends activation times. The check also fails the whole flag with `PARSE_ERROR` when one activation string does not match the strict parser, even for a subject without a timestamp. Exclusion in immediate mode does not need activation times.
Evidence — measured cost with opt-out off, and the PARSE_ERROR Minimum ns per evaluation over 3 interleaved rounds, Node 24, mode `false` (the node-server default): | flag | this PR | with the fix | | --- | ---: | ---: | | JSON, 5 allocations, 3 with activation | 3,570–3,618 | 2,244–2,261 | | fixture `integer-flag` | 2,199–2,207 | 1,407–1,412 | | protobuf, 5 allocations | 310–311 | 256–262 | With the fix, the first row is in the same range as the same flag without activation fields (2,229–2,269 ns). With opt-out off, an activation of `2026-10-01 12:00:00Z` or `2026-10-01T12:00:00+0000` makes the flag return the default with `PARSE_ERROR`. The edge parses activation with chrono `DateTime` (serde), and chrono 0.4.45 accepts both strings. I have not seen the backend emit either form; the compiler change that adds the field (ddoghq/dd-source#139381) is not merged.
Suggested fix — gate both up-front checks on future mode ```diff diff --git a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts index 5879d3c..eb3b3e0 100644 --- a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts +++ b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts @@ -61,6 +61,8 @@ export function evaluateForSubject( const now = new Date(evaluationTimestampMs) if ( + typeof excludeExperiments === 'object' && + excludeExperiments.mode === 'future_experiments_only' && flag.allocations.some( (allocation) => allocation.randomizationActivatedAt != null && !parseOptOutInstant(allocation.randomizationActivatedAt) diff --git a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts index 1055b69..4579b93 100644 --- a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts +++ b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts @@ -75,6 +75,8 @@ export function evaluateProtobufConfiguration( } if ( + typeof excludeExperiments === 'object' && + excludeExperiments.mode === 'future_experiments_only' && flag.allocations.some( ({ randomizationActivatedAt: activation }) => activation && ```
Tests — a new file that fails against this PR `packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out-activation.test.ts`: ```ts import { evaluateRulesBasedConfiguration } from './evaluation' import type { UniversalFlagConfigurationV1 } from './ufc-v1' const logger = { debug: jest.fn(), info: jest.fn(), warn: jest.fn(), error: jest.fn() } function rules(activation: string): UniversalFlagConfigurationV1 { return { createdAt: '2026-10-20T00:00:00Z', format: 'SERVER', environment: { name: 'test' }, flags: { flag: { key: 'flag', enabled: true, variationType: 'BOOLEAN', variations: { on: { key: 'on', value: true }, off: { key: 'off', value: false } }, allocations: [ { key: 'ordinary', doLog: false, splits: [{ variationKey: 'on', shards: [] }] }, { key: 'experiment', doLog: true, randomizationActivatedAt: activation, splits: [{ variationKey: 'off', shards: [] }], }, ], }, }, } } describe('activation the edge accepts, default mode', () => { it.each(['2026-10-01 12:00:00Z', '2026-10-01T12:00:00+0000'])('%s does not fail the flag', (activation) => { const result = evaluateRulesBasedConfiguration( rules(activation), 'boolean', 'flag', false, { targetingKey: 's' }, logger ) expect(result).toMatchObject({ value: true }) expect(result.errorCode).toBeUndefined() }) }) ```
Verification — what I ran - Both new tests fail against this PR and pass with the fix. - The existing `rejects malformed activation on the affected flag, including unreachable allocations` still passes, because it runs in future mode. Deleting the check instead fails that test, so I kept the check and gated it. - Core 996/996, browser 516/516, node-server 531/531 in the batch with the other suggestions from this review.

🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P2]** Treat a missing `doLog` as `true` for exposures too, and add a test for a missing `doLog`. This line treats an allocation without `doLog` as an experiment (`allocation.doLog !== false`). That matches the edge, where `doLog` defaults to `true`. The result metadata on lines 125 and 130 uses `!!allocation.doLog`, so the same allocation logs no exposure for an eligible subject. That predates this PR, but now one function reads `doLog` two ways. No test distinguishes `!== false` from `=== true` on this line.
Evidence — the two readings, and the untested line - Allocation without `doLog`, eligible subject: value from that allocation, metadata `doLog: false`, so no exposure. - Same allocation, opted-out subject in `Immediate` mode: skipped as an experiment. - Edge: `#[serde(default = "default_do_log")] pub do_log: bool` with `default_do_log() -> true` (`domains/ffe/libs/flagging/rust/evaluation/src/rules_based/ufc/models.rs`, ddoghq/dd-source#140422 head). - Changing `!== false` to `=== true` on this line passes all 992 core tests.
Suggested fix — read doLog the edge way in the metadata ```diff diff --git a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts index 5879d3c..eb3b3e0 100644 --- a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts +++ b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts @@ -122,12 +124,12 @@ export function evaluateForSubject( ...createEvaluationTimestampMetadata(evaluationTimestampMs), // Keys for dd-trace-js __dd_allocation_key: allocation.key, - __dd_do_log: !!allocation.doLog, + __dd_do_log: allocation.doLog !== false, __dd_split_serial_id: selectedSplit.serialId, // Legacy keys (internal) - to be removed from server-side allocationKey: allocation.key, variationType: variantTypeToFlagValueType(flag.variationType), - doLog: !!allocation.doLog, + doLog: allocation.doLog !== false, } as PrecomputedFlagMetadata, } } ```
Test — append to experimentation-opt-out-future.test.ts ```diff diff --git a/packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out-future.test.ts b/packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out-future.test.ts index 0c5e887..fb1cb06 100644 --- a/packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out-future.test.ts +++ b/packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out-future.test.ts @@ -151,3 +151,15 @@ it.each([ expect(acknowledgesExperimentationOptOut(configuration, policy)).toBe(expected) expect(compareOptOutInstants(parseOptOutInstant(cutoff)!, parseOptOutInstant(timestamp)!) === 0).toBe(expected) }) + +it.each(['immediate', mode] as const)( + 'treats a JSON allocation without doLog as an experiment in %s mode', + (policy) => { + const json = jsonRules(cutoff) + delete json.flags.flag.allocations[0].doLog + expect(evaluateRulesBasedConfiguration(json, 'boolean', 'flag', true, context, logger, policy).value).toBe(false) + expect( + evaluateRulesBasedConfiguration(json, 'boolean', 'flag', false, { targetingKey: 'subject' }, logger, policy) + ).toMatchObject({ value: true, flagMetadata: { doLog: true, __dd_do_log: true } }) + } +) ```
Verification — what I ran - Core 996/996 in the batch with the other suggestions from this review. - The test fails against this PR's metadata (2 cases) and against the `=== true` mutant (2 cases).

🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **Heads up:** if a customer enables a mode before ddoghq/dd-source#140422 is deployed, an opted-out subject gets the default for every flag. Without ddoghq/dd-source#140422, the edge request deserializer skips `evaluation_options` and returns 200 without an acknowledgement. This line then throws `ParseError`. Unless an acknowledged cached snapshot exists for that context, the provider emits `PROVIDER_ERROR`, ordinary flags and experiments both return the default, and nothing retries until the next context change. I trust you to sequence the deploys. This records the failure mode, which differs across the three SDKs.
Evidence — what each SDK reports when the response has no acknowledgement | SDK | flags return | state / event | retry | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | JS (this PR) | default, `INVALID_CONTEXT` | `PROVIDER_ERROR` from the rejected context change | next context change | | Android, native client | default, `PROVIDER_NOT_READY` | `FlagsClientState.Error` | next context change | | Android, OpenFeature provider | `PROVIDER_FATAL` for every flag once the client is FATAL | `ProviderError` carrying `ProviderFatalError` | a later successful context change, or a ready or stale event | | iOS | default, `providerNotReady` | `.error`; completion `.invalidResponse` | next context change | Measured with each SDK against a 200 response that has no `evaluation_options`, for an eligible-to-opted-out change with no cached snapshot. In JS the fetch count was 3 across initialize, the opted-out change, and the change back. Before ddoghq/dd-source#140422, the deserializer skips unknown fields through `_ => map.next_value::()`. That PR adds an explicit `evaluation_options` arm ahead of it.

🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **Heads up:** this file overlaps DataDog/openfeature-js-client#420, and the two PRs validate the timestamp differently. DataDog/openfeature-js-client#420 adds its own `hasExperimentationOptOut` to this file and validates with `new Date(value)` ("Use the same timestamp parser as allocation startAt and endAt"); its `evaluation.ts` uses that function. This PR's `evaluation.ts` uses `experimentationOptOutPolicy`, which calls the strict `parseOptOutInstant`. Resolving the conflict picks one rule for both packages, which can change which timestamps return `INVALID_CONTEXT` for the other one. An in-memory merge of the two heads conflicts in six core files and the fixture pin. The two mode enums can stay package-specific (`Default` exists only in node-server, `FutureExperimentsOnly` only here). One shared timestamp parser in `flagging-core` would keep validation consistent.
Evidence — git merge-tree of 5e9709b and cc3555d ```text packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluation.ts packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out.test.ts (add/add) packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out.ts (add/add) packages/core/test/evaluation/flags-v1.spec.ts packages/core/test/ffe-system-test-data (submodule) ```

🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P3]** Make `parseOptOutInstant` accept what the edge accepts, and parse activation with the edge's activation grammar. The edge parses `dd_experimentation_opt_out_at` with chrono 0.4.45 `DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339`, and `randomizationActivatedAt` with chrono's serde `DateTime`, which accepts more. On a 47-row table, this parser rejects 7 inputs that chrono accepts: a space separator, leap seconds (`:60`), and a U+2212 minus in the offset. Activation strings use the same strict parser.
Evidence — rows where this parser and chrono disagree | input | chrono 0.4.45 | JS (this PR) | | --- | --- | --- | | `2025-01-01 00:00:00Z` (space separator) | accept | reject | | `2016-12-31T23:59:60Z` (leap second) | accept | reject | | `2016-12-31T23:59:60.5Z` | accept | reject | | `2016-12-31T23:59:60.999999999Z` | accept | reject | | `2025-06-15T12:34:60Z` (leap second, any minute) | accept | reject | | `2017-01-01T00:59:60+01:00` | accept | reject | | `2025-01-01T00:00:00−05:00` (U+2212 minus) | accept | reject | For activation, chrono's serde parser also accepts `2026-10-01T12:00:00+0000`, `2026-10-01T12:00:00 +00:00` and `2026-10-01T12:00:00 UTC`. chrono orders a leap second after `:59.999999999` and before the next `:00`. One edge case stays: `0000-01-01T00:00:00+01:00` is a valid cutoff, but the edge echoes it as `-0001-12-31T23:00:00Z`, which `parse_from_rfc3339` rejects. So a future-mode acknowledgement for a cutoff whose UTC instant falls outside years 0000–9999 never matches, in all three SDKs. Rejecting such cutoffs at the edge would close it.
Suggested fix — a chrono-compatible parser, and a serde-compatible one for activation `OptOutInstant` becomes `{ seconds, nanos }`, with a leap second as second 59 plus 1e9 ns. The cache key becomes `mode:seconds:nanos`. ```diff diff --git a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts index 5879d3c..3d0a695 100644 --- a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts +++ b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateForSubject.ts @@ -3,7 +3,7 @@ import type { FlagTypeToValue, PrecomputedFlagMetadata } from '../configuration' import { type TimeStamp, timeStampNow } from '../time' import { TargetingKeyMissingError } from './errors' import { createEvaluationTimestampMetadata } from './evaluationMetadata' -import { type ExperimentationOptOutPolicy, excludesExperiment, parseOptOutInstant } from './experimentation-opt-out' +import { type ExperimentationOptOutPolicy, excludesExperiment, parseActivationInstant } from './experimentation-opt-out' import { matchesShard } from './matchesShard' import { isValidRule, matchesRule, type Rule } from './rules' import { type Flag, type Split, type VariantType, variantTypeToFlagValueType } from './ufc-v1' @@ -63,7 +63,7 @@ export function evaluateForSubject( if ( flag.allocations.some( (allocation) => - allocation.randomizationActivatedAt != null && !parseOptOutInstant(allocation.randomizationActivatedAt) + allocation.randomizationActivatedAt != null && !parseActivationInstant(allocation.randomizationActivatedAt) ) ) { return { value: defaultValue, reason: 'ERROR', errorCode: 'PARSE_ERROR' as ErrorCode } diff --git a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts index 1055b69..9d015cb 100644 --- a/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts +++ b/packages/core/src/evaluation/evaluateProtobufConfiguration.ts @@ -91,10 +91,7 @@ export function evaluateProtobufConfiguration( if (excludeExperiments && allocation.logExposureEvent) { const activation = allocation.randomizationActivatedAt if (excludeExperiments === true || excludeExperiments.mode === 'immediate') continue - const instant = activation && { - seconds: Number(activation.seconds), - fraction: String(activation.nanos).padStart(9, '0'), - } + const instant = activation && { seconds: Number(activation.seconds), nanos: activation.nanos } if (excludesExperimentAt(excludeExperiments, true, instant)) continue } if (!matchesCondition(allocation.targetingConditionIndex, configuration, context, conditionResults)) { diff --git a/packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out.ts b/packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out.ts index 7b419e2..ff37e2e 100644 --- a/packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out.ts +++ b/packages/core/src/evaluation/experimentation-opt-out.ts @@ -5,43 +5,79 @@ export type ExperimentationOptOutModeValue = 'disabled' | 'immediate' | 'future_ export type ExperimentationOptOutOption = boolean | ExperimentationOptOutModeValue export interface OptOutInstant { seconds: number - fraction: string + /** 0 to 1,999,999,999; values from 1e9 are a leap second, as in chrono. */ + nanos: number } export type ExperimentationOptOutPolicy = false | { mode: 'immediate' | 'future_experiments_only'; cutoff: OptOutInstant } -/** Compare complete instants without losing fractional precision in JavaScript Date. */ +// The edge parses the subject's cutoff with chrono `DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339`. +const RFC3339 = + /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})[Tt ](\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})(?:\.(\d+))?(?:[Zz]|([+\-\u2212])(\d{2}):([0-5]\d))$/ +// Rust `char::is_whitespace`; unlike JS `\s`, it includes U+0085 and excludes U+FEFF. +const RUST_SPACE = String.raw`\t-\r \x85\u00a0\u1680\u2000-\u200a\u2028\u2029\u202f\u205f\u3000` +const SPACES = `[${RUST_SPACE}]*` +// The edge parses UFC `randomizationActivatedAt` with chrono's relaxed `DateTime` serde/FromStr grammar. +const RELAXED_RFC3339 = new RegExp( + String.raw`^${SPACES}([+-]\d+|\d{1,4})${SPACES}-${SPACES}(\d{1,2})${SPACES}-${SPACES}(\d{1,2})[Tt ]${SPACES}(\d{1,2})${SPACES}:${SPACES}(\d{1,2})${SPACES}:${SPACES}(\d{1,2})(?:\.(\d+))?${SPACES}(?:[Uu][Tt][Cc]|[Zz]|([+\-\u2212])(\d{2})[:${RUST_SPACE}]*([0-5]\d))${SPACES}$` +) +// chrono supports years -262143 to 262142. +const MIN_YEAR = -262143 +const MAX_YEAR = 262142 +const MIN_SECONDS = daysFromCivil(MIN_YEAR, 1, 1) * 86400 +const MAX_SECONDS = daysFromCivil(MAX_YEAR, 12, 31) * 86400 + 86399 + +/** Accepts exactly what the edge accepts for `dd_experimentation_opt_out_at`, at nanosecond precision. */ export function parseOptOutInstant(value: unknown): OptOutInstant | undefined { - if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined - const match = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})[Tt](\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})(?:\.(\d+))?([Zz]|([+-])(\d{2}):(\d{2}))$/.exec( - value - ) + return typeof value === 'string' ? toInstant(RFC3339.exec(value)) : undefined +} + +/** Accepts exactly what the edge accepts for an allocation's `randomizationActivatedAt`. */ +export function parseActivationInstant(value: unknown): OptOutInstant | undefined { + return typeof value === 'string' ? toInstant(RELAXED_RFC3339.exec(value)) : undefined +} + +function toInstant(match: RegExpExecArray | null): OptOutInstant | undefined { if (!match) return undefined - comments.author: leoromanovsky
comments.body: Thank you but this is not relevant to what we are building here. If I was to change it, my reading of the open feature spec is that `RECONCILING` is more appropriate.

comments.author: leoromanovsky
comments.body: Moved validation to configuration preparation in [8a3e76c](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/commit/8a3e76c679ac290eb06c43936597c241029199b3). Evaluation reuses the parsed timestamp. This avoids repeated parsing and keeps validation independent of opt-out mode, so other consumers can safely use the field later.

comments.author: leoromanovsky
comments.body: `doLog` is required by the [UFC schema](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/blob/d1f74a5e6e524b93637df56a37bcc9c63f852b37/domains/remote-config/shared/libs/config-validator/schemas/FFE_FLAGS/root.json#L134), and the producer always emits an explicit boolean. Made that requirement explicit in the JS allocation type in [826386e](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/commit/826386e7b38df50007d56ff1d7ce046ef0fb97c2). Changes to missing-field defaults can be handled separately.

comments.body: We're keeping parsing simple around a canonical timestamp format supported across Rust, Node.js, and Go. We’ll document and test that supported subset rather than reproduce Chrono’s permissive extensions. The same format applies to activation timestamps.

comments.body: Documented and enforced that subset in [a96b572](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/commit/a96b5726a767bfb4acf3adbfda4b6909947f0508). Cutoffs and JSON activation share one parser; excess precision is rejected instead of silently truncated. Activation validation still happens once at configuration receipt.

comments.body: Updated in [3704387](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/commit/3704387fc1f33220ffe261539aff59d4e3bb1e6d). A valid context waiting for usable assignments now returns `PROVIDER_NOT_READY`, including after a failed refresh. Malformed input keeps `INVALID_CONTEXT`, and configuration parse errors are preserved. Tests cover both enabled modes through the OpenFeature client.

comments.body: Scoped this in [3704387](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/commit/3704387fc1f33220ffe261539aff59d4e3bb1e6d): invalid activation fails the flag only for an opted-out subject in future mode. Parsing still happens once on receipt, with explicit valid/missing/invalid states so future consumers cannot mistake invalid metadata for missing metadata. The canonical timestamp format stays as agreed.

comments.body:
Updated in [38d611c](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/commit/38d611cf4c73b9687b97f7da0f8224d2fefab966). The parser now accepts lowercase `t`/`z` and truncates fractional digits beyond nanoseconds without rounding. Subject cutoffs, JSON activation, and acknowledgements share that normalization. Docs and tests cover the accepted forms, timezone offsets, and nanosecond boundaries.

You were also right about JavaScript's `$` anchor; the incorrect comment and redundant check were removed in [22d0fd4](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/commit/22d0fd427b471abb99d85c7ab4d922836d2bc29a).
